questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

Detailed Solution:
